daily_brief: The day's most consequential developments center on the unprecedented trilateral summit between Presidents Trump, Xi, and Putin in Shenzhen, with the three leaders meeting for the first time together ahead of Thursday's formal talks [BBC], [Nikkei Asia], [The Hindu]. The summit has drawn comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference, though officials are tempering expectations of immediate breakthroughs on Ukraine or Iran [Le Monde], [The Economist]. Meanwhile, tensions between the US and Iran escalated as Iran targeted American military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain following US strikes on Qeshm Island, raising fears of broader conflict [BBC], [Al Jazeera], [The Hindu]. In a significant blow to Russian logistics, Ukraine executed a multi-stage operation that collapsed a key span of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea [BBC], [Al Jazeera], [The Hindu]. On the technology front, Nvidia reported surging revenues of $116 billion while firmly rejecting ousted founder Jensen Huang's bid to return as CEO [BBC], [RNZ]. In US politics, Democrat Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska's Senate race completed a historic midterm sweep, giving Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority [France 24], [ABC Australia].

top_stories.headline: Trump, Xi, and Putin Gather in Shenzhen for Historic Three-Way Summit
bullets: Trump arrived in Shenzhen where Xi Jinping greeted him on the tarmac; Trump later exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of Thursday's trilateral meeting
The three leaders will discuss Ukraine, Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions, and AI development; this marks the first time the US, Chinese, and Russian leaders have met together in person
Xi described China-Russia relations as 'a source of stability' in a 'turbulent world' during bilateral talks with Putin on Wednesday
Officials have downplayed expectations for substantive outcomes, describing the summit as more exploratory and symbolic

top_stories.headline: Iran Strikes US Bases in Kuwait and Bahrain as Gulf Tensions Escalate
bullets: Iran's military targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase in Kuwait and facilities in Bahrain overnight, marking the first attack on Kuwait in over two months
The strikes followed US warplane attacks on an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday
A UAE oil tanker crew member is missing after an attack in the Gulf waterway; at least 17 vessels have been attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July
Analysts warn the current 'frozen war' status quo is inherently unstable and could escalate into full-blown conflict

sources.framing_note: Emphasized that the US and Israel initiated the conflict in February; noted Tehran's perspective on provocations

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Executes Multi-Stage Operation to Collapse Key Span of Crimean Bridge
bullets: A weeks-long Ukrainian operation systematically destroyed Russian air defenses before launching coordinated drone and missile strikes that collapsed a road bridge arch
President Zelenskyy confirmed Ukrainian-made Neptune and Flamingo missiles along with heavy drones were used in the 'unprecedented operation'
Road traffic is suspended and rail services restricted to one track; approximately 200 meters of roadway was heavily damaged and submerged
Russia's Kremlin spokesman said the bridge 'will be rebuilt' but analysts note Crimea is 'logistically turning into an island'

sources.framing_note: Detailed technical breakdown of the seven-stage operation

sources.framing_note: Provided historical context on previous bridge attacks since 2022

top_stories.headline: Nvidia Reports Doubled Revenue to $116 Billion, Rules Out Huang's Return as CEO
bullets: Nvidia reported quarterly sales of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, with profits doubling to $65 billion
Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors 'we've got this' in the company's first results since founder Jensen Huang's departure
Board chair Harvey Jones firmly rejected Huang's public statement that he would be 'honoured' to return, saying the board 'does not intend to reinstate him'
The company forecast revenue of $130 billion next quarter despite assuming no data-center chip sales to China

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on corporate governance drama and financial performance

top_stories.headline: Democrat Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Race, Completing Historic Midterm Sweep
bullets: Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan with slightly over 50% of the vote after two weeks of ballot counting
The victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority after flipping nine GOP-held seats, their best midterm performance since 1958
Democrats also won Senate races in conservative states including South Carolina, Texas, Kansas, and Mississippi
Peltola overcame allegations that her campaign helped recruit an independent candidate sharing the Republican incumbent's name
